history.summary: IMPORTANT IDENTITY NOTE: No published travel, tourism, or temple source documents a specific 'Kali Mandir' in Williamnagar; the identity, exact location, age, and history of this shrine could not be verified from web or social sources, so this entry should be treated as provisional (verify). Williamnagar is the planned district headquarters town of East Garo Hills on the Simsang (Simsanggre) plain, named after Captain Williamson A. Sangma, Meghalaya's first chief minister; the area is historically noted for the Garos' last major resistance to the British in 1837 (legendary leader Pa Togan Nengminja Sangma fell at Chisobibra, 12 December 1837). The Garo Hills are today overwhelmingly Christian, and Hindu shrines in the region are generally small, community-serving temples of the non-tribal population (Bengali, Nepali, Assamese, Hindi-speaking) rather than historic pilgrimage sites; the best-known Hindu temple of the region is the Tura Thakurbari in West Garo Hills (~76 km away). A generic 'Temple' geotagged at Samanda, very close to Williamnagar, appears on map listings, but no name, deity, or history is attached to it (verify whether this is the CSV shrine). Do not conflate this entry with the Kali temples of Assam (Dudhnai, Balijana, Goalpara) or with Dakshineswar/Kalighat in Kolkata, which surfaced in searches but are hundreds of kilometres away.

name: Kali Mandir
town_description: Williamnagar is a planned town on the Simsang river plain and the headquarters of East Garo Hills district, Meghalaya, named after Captain Williamson A. Sangma, the state's first chief minister. About 313 km from Shillong and 76 km from Tura, it sits in historically significant country where the Garos made their last major resistance to British intrusion in 1837. Nearby attractions include the Simsang river, Rongbang Dare waterfall and the Nokrek and Balphakram national parks further afield.

travel.airport: Nearest airport with scheduled commercial flights: Lokpriya Gopinath Bordoloi International Airport, Guwahati, Assam (approx. 170-200 km by road; verify). The Tura/Baljek airstrip (approx. 76 km) has no regular commercial services (verify).
travel.railway: Guwahati railway station, Assam, is the nearest major railhead (approx. 170-200 km by road; verify); onward by bus or taxi via Tura/Paikan or via Shillong.
travel.road: Williamnagar is approx. 313 km from Shillong and approx. 76 km from Tura; connected by state highways with bus and shared-taxi services from Shillong, Tura and Guwahati (verify current routes).

visitor_information.best_time: October to March (generally October-May is the best season for Williamnagar); Kali Puja around Diwali (October-November) would be the most significant time for a Kali shrine (verify).
